Key Research Thinking Patterns: Within-Person Dynamics: Focuses on how variables change over time within a single individual, rather than comparing differences between people (e.g., used a 10-day study to model the reciprocal, daily influence between job boredom and counterproductive work behavior).

Moderated Mediation: Explains how an effect occurs via a mediator and when that indirect effect changes depending on a moderator (e.g. showed that overqualification leads to less helpful behavior via boredom, but this effect was buffered for those with a strong career calling).

Ecological Momentary Intervention: Delivers real-time interventions to participants in their natural envrionments to test causal effects (e.g. randomly sent employees real-time emotion regulation exercises during workday to prove exercises caused a reduction in negative effect).

Scale Development and Validation: Created and tested a set of questions to ensure it accurately measures the psychological construct in question (e.g. created and validated new 25-item scale to reliably measure six facets of worker attitudes toward AI).
Summary Description: JeongJin Kim is a researcher in organizational psychology and affective science with a notable focus on the within-person dynamics of employee emotions and their real-world impact. His work innovatively examines the daily fluctuations of states like job boredom and attitudes toward AI, connecting them to outcomes like burnout and counterproductive behaviors. Kim's research consistently features rigorous longitudinal methods, including daily diary studies and ecological momentary interventions, analyzed with advanced techniques like latent change score modeling. He emphasizes developing validated scales and empirically testing underlying affective mechanisms to provide data-driven insights into the modern workplace experience.
